scope: repository tooling, phase evidence, task routing, identity/profile artifacts, and local execution

attack_paths.path: prompt injection -> tool misuse -> secret or private record disclosure
attack_paths.control: treat documents as data; private-material scan; no raw excerpts
attack_paths.residual: manual review can miss novel encodings

attack_paths.path: route spoofing -> false sibling completion -> premature next phase
attack_paths.control: live task tool receipt plus one-message state machine
attack_paths.residual: route availability and task semantics require supervision

attack_paths.path: shared-branch mutation -> provenance loss or sibling overwrite
attack_paths.control: owned worktrees, exact staging, remote equality

attack_paths.path: dependency or script compromise -> unexpected code execution
attack_paths.control: standard-library-first bounded scripts, review diffs, no automatic downloads

attack_paths.path: memory poisoning -> stale routing or false canon
attack_paths.control: live user request outranks notes and historical beacons
attack_paths.residual: ambiguous prompts can still require judgment

attack_paths.path: destructive cleanup -> loss of evidence or worktrees
attack_paths.control: exact destructive gate and no automatic cleanup
typed claims, evidence grades, open-gap and exact-gate labels

incident_sequence: preserve logs without publishing private data
